questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration of a Particle Moving With Circular Motion
questions.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j)$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(3(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-6\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+6\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-12\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i-12\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-12\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}+(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{144{cos}^{2}⁡2t+144{sin}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{144} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $12\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Note that $||a||$ is constant, but $a$ is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
a=-{\omega }^{2}r\,⇒\,||a||={\omega }^{2}||r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $a=3\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||a||={2}^{2}\cdot 3=12\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity and Speed of a Particle Moving With Circular Motion
questions.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(5\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-10\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+10\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-10\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+(10\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100{sin}^{2}⁡2t+100{cos}^{2}⁡2t} \\  & =\sqrt{100({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the object is $10\text{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||v||=R|\omega |,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega $ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=5\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||v||=5\cdot |2|=10\text{ m/s}.
$$

questions.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $1\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(5,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $R=5$ and $\omega =1\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =5(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(5(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the velocity vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,j \\  & =-5\,i\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(4,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the velocity of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{8}$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $R=4$ and $\omega =2\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =4(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(4(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the velocity vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{8},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})\,j \\  & =-8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\,j \\  & =-\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{2}\,i+\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{2}\,j \\  & =-4\sqrt{2}\,i+4\sqrt{2}\,j\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $0.5\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(4,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\pi $ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $a$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=a(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(a,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $a=4$ and $\omega =\frac{1}{2}\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =4\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & ={(4\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,j)}^{′} \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,j \\ a(t) & ={(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,j)}^{′} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{t}{2}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\pi ) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,j \\  & =-\,j\end{aligned}
$$
